overview.description: Euchre is the classic American partnership trick-taking game, played with a 24-32 card deck. Its hallmark feature is the 'Bower' system: the Jack of the called trump suit (Right Bower) and the Jack of the same-colored suit (Left Bower) are the two highest trump cards. Teams of two bid for the right to name trump and must win 3 of 5 tricks; failure results in being 'Euchred' and the opponent scoring 2 points. First team to 10 points wins.
overview.deck: 24 cards (9, 10, J, Q, K, A in 4 suits)

history.origins: Euchre developed in the early 19th century American Midwest. It is believed to derive from 'Jucker' or 'Juckerspiel,' a card game played by German immigrants in Pennsylvania, Ohio, and Indiana. It was the dominant American card game before Poker took over in the late 19th century.
timeline: 1820s-1840s: Euchre documented in the American Midwest.
1850s-1880s: Most popular card game in the United States.
Late 1800s: Displaced by Poker as America's premier card game.
Present: Regional staple in the Great Lakes region (Ohio, Michigan, Indiana). Also popular in Canada and parts of UK/Australia.
history.evolution: Euchre gave English-language card play the term 'Bower' (from German 'Bauer'=farmer/Jack) and the word 'Euchred' (deceived/defeated). The Joker was also originally introduced in American decks specifically for Euchre.
history.cultural: A keystone of American Midwest social culture. Church halls, senior centers, and community leagues in Ohio and Michigan regularly run Euchre tournaments. Also beloved in Great Lakes Canada.

setup.deck: 24 cards: 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in each of 4 suits (Euchre deck). Some use 28 (add 7s and 8s) or 32 cards.
setup.equipment: 24-card Euchre deck. Score markers or score paper.
setup.dealing: 5 cards each in batches (2+3 or 3+2). Remaining 4 cards are the Kitty; top card turned face-up.

rules.objective: Win at least 3 of 5 tricks with your partner; first team to 10 or 11 points wins the game.
rules.gameplay: Players bid to make trump suit, then play tricks. The making team must win at least 3 tricks to score points. Special trump cards (bowers and aces) rank highest. Players can choose to play alone for higher scoring potential.
keyRules: Right Bower (trump Jack) is the HIGHEST trump card.
Left Bower (matching-color Jack) is the SECOND highest trump card and IS trump suit (not its original suit).
Being Euchred = losing team scores 2 points.

strategy.basic: Bower Power: Only order up if you hold the Right Bower, OR the Left Bower plus Ace of trump. Ordering up with 2 small trump and no Bower is very risky.
strategy.intermediate: Suit Control: Pay attention to the suits your partner playsâ€”if they lead a high off-suit card, they likely have a void in trump (signaling strength). Counter-order: Order up from the 3rd or 4th seat only if you can cover your partnerâ€”the 4th-seat order is the safest.
strategy.advanced: Going Alone Threshold: Go alone with Right Bower + Left Bower + Ace of trump + any other trump = near-certain sweep. Any less and the Euchre risk is high. Partner Signals: The opening lead of the highest card in a suit signals a void in that suit (asking partner to trump it).
tips: 'Never order up the first round in seat 1 or 2 unless you have 3+ trump.'
The Left Bower is a trumpâ€”don't confuse it for off-suit when leading.

phases.label: Declare Trump Suit

phases.label: Play Tricks
phases.notes: Players play 5 tricks following suit when possible; highest card or trump wins each trick.

deal.reason: Cards dealt automatically by dealer at start of hand.

declare.description: Declare the trump suit or pass.
declare.constraints: Players declare in order; first to declare makes trump and their team are makers.

award_pot.reason: No pot; winner determined by game rules.

play_card.constraints: Must follow suit. Left Bower is trump suit.

pass.description: Pass without taking another action this turn.
pass.constraints: Allowed when rules permit skipping a wager or play.

engine.rankingSystem: Trump: Right Bower > Left Bower > A > K > Q > 10 > 9. Off-suit: A > K > Q > J > 10 > 9.
engine.deckDescription: Standard 24-card Euchre deck: twenty-four cards comprising the 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, and Ace in each of four French suits; no jokers in the basic game.
engine.suitDescription: French suit set: four suits—Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, and Clubs—each with six cards (9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace) in this stripped Euchre deck.
engine.rankDescription: Stripped twenty-four rank set: 9 (low), 10, Jack, Queen, King, and Ace (high), with six cards per suit; Jack of trump is right bower, same-color Jack is left bower.

synthesis.shortDescription: The American Midwest's defining card game and ancestor of the Joker. Partnership trick-taking where Jacks rule as Bowers, trumps are chosen by bidding, and failing to win 3 tricks earns the dreaded Euchre. Race to 10 points.
